idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy - rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after v2.3.1 was deployed to production (us-east, us-west, eu-west). Error rate was 0.18 on v2.3.1. Action taken: rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all production regions, the most recent release with a healthy production history. Post-rollback status: all three regions on v2.3.0, healthy=true, error rate 0.002. v2.3.1 is marked unhealthy in production and v2.3.1-rc was unhealthy in staging. Follow-up: investigate the v2.3.1 failure before any redeploy; v2.3.1 has never been healthy in production, so redeploying it requires change-manager approval.

trace.final:
checkout-api is rolled back to v2.3.0 in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), and the service is healthy again. Error rate dropped from 0.18 on v2.3.1 to 0.002.

- **Rollback target:** v2.3.0 was the most recent release with a healthy production status. v2.3.1 was the failing release, and it has never been healthy in production, so no change-manager approval was needed for the rollback.
- **Incident:** SEV2 incident **INC-0001** is open for checkout-api and has paged on-call. The first attempt to create it timed out, so I retried with the same idempotency key. The incident was created once.
- **Follow-up:** v2.3.1 needs investigation before anyone redeploys it. Any future deploy of v2.3.1 will need change-manager approval until it has a healthy production record.

content.text: The most recent production release that was healthy is v2.3.0. v2.3.1 is the unhealthy one currently running in all three regions. I'll roll back to v2.3.0, which has a healthy production history, so it doesn't need change-manager approval.
The rollback is confirmed healthy. Next I'll open the SEV2 incident.
